summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, fatigue, dry cough, myalgias, and arthralgias in the setting of relapsed multiple myeloma and recent cytopenias. Initial evaluation revealed no bacterial infection, with negative blood, urine, and stool cultures, and imaging showing no pneumonia or new abdominal pathology. His symptoms were attributed to a viral syndrome. He developed transient abdominal pain and minor gastrointestinal bleeding, but CT abdomen/pelvis was unremarkable except for stable known findings. Renal function improved with IV hydration, and he received one unit of red blood cells for anemia and platelets for thrombocytopenia. His condition stabilized, fever resolved, and he was discharged home in improved condition with plans to follow up with oncology and resume chemotherapy as advised.
